title: Midnight Club LA Remix
notes: Read from PSPASSET.DAT (DAVE archive, 'psppck' memory images) with the Midnight Club LA Remix toolkit (dave_extract / mcla_psp / mcla_export).

The 49 player cars and bikes of the game.  Folder names are the game's file codes without the 'vp_' prefix (maker_model_year; '_dub' = the DUB Edition cars; d_tokyo_cop_01 = the Tokyo police car, impalass_cop_s_96 = the L.A. police car; 'destroy' is called vp_destroy in the game).

A car is its stock set: body shell with windows and interior, stock hood / bumpers / side skirts / spoiler / trunk / lamps, exhaust tips, suspension arms and 4 wheels.  Rim, tyre and brake discs / calipers are separate objects (stock rim, tyre and brake of the car's .carcfg, sized by its RimSize).

KITS: every optional part of the game (hoods, bumpers, skirts, spoilers, lamps, blowers, side exhausts and the complete wide-body set) is in the hidden 'Variants' folder of <car>.fbx (a subfolder per kind of part) and, to be seen, in <car>_kits.fbx: the stock car and then one complete car per kit style (kit_1, kit_2 ... kit_wide), all VISIBLE, in rows of 6.

Paint is a run time shader in the game: one plain red for all (like the Forza sets).  Left out: ground shadow, neon glow, light cones, the blur discs of spinning wheels, the vinyl decal cards (white rectangles that the game covers with the player's vinyls) and the lower levels of detail of the police cars.  The pictures of this PSP game are tiny (mostly 64 x 64 atlases).  Windows are 50 % see-through.
Tyre sizes are the toolkit's approximation of the game's RimSize / TireProfile logic (tyre radius = height of the wheel node; the bike tyres look fat).

RIMS: the folder _Rims holds every rim of the game (rim.pspppf: 320 of 322 slots, two are empty), one rim per folder, scaled to a 19 inch rim, standing on the ground, outer face towards +X.  The number is the slot of the rim pack, the name is the game's own (whl_stk_<car> = the stock rim of a car).  Tyres, brakes and exhausts are not included as files of their own.

TRAFFIC: the folder _Traffic holds the 38 traffic vehicles (taxis, buses, trucks, police, ambulance, the Tokyo train ...), high detail level. _usage.csv tells where the game's own traffic files use each of them: in L.A. / in Tokyo, switched off (count 0) or not at all (left over from Midnight Club 3: the Atlanta and Detroit variants).  Tokyo_leftovers.txt: what the archive holds about Tokyo (the game's bonus second city) and what of it is unused.

Fixes in the toolkit's parser (the fixed copies are mcla_psp.py / mcla_export.py next to the scripts): its texture cache was keyed by the id() of Python objects (reused after garbage collection, so some rims got the logo of another part); 9 rim slots keep their batch table 0x34 bytes after the mesh instead of 0x44 (unreadable before); the standalone .tex pictures of 358 files (all body pictures of the traffic vehicles) were not decoded; the picture coordinates of the binary traffic meshes are column 4 of the Adj table, not column 3 (that gave stripes); and the text meshes of the Atlanta / Detroit traffic vehicles use a second strip type, TRISTRIP2, which was read as a triangle list.
